summary: Kisspeptin is a peptide in the growth factors & reproductive class (KISS1 receptor agonist; GnRH release). Europe PMC indexes 3,850 publications naming it or a listed alias in a title or abstract, including 44 randomized controlled trials and 34 clinical trials of any design, as of 2026-09-14. The strongest evidence tier in that literature is human clinical trials. This page reports what those studies state, sentence by sentence, with each statement tied to its source and labeled by the kind of evidence it is. It does not recommend use, and it does not translate study doses into anything personal.

faq.question: Has Kisspeptin been tested in humans?
faq.answer: Yes. Europe PMC indexes 34 clinical trials and 44 randomized controlled trials naming Kisspeptin or a listed alias in the title or abstract. The evidence table above lists the ones in this record's ledger with their design and sample size; check the study name, since an alias can refer to a different formulation of the same molecule.

faq.question: What kind of evidence exists for Kisspeptin?
faq.answer: The strongest tier is human clinical trial: human clinical trials. Every claim on this page carries its own tier, because a compound with one human trial and forty animal studies is described by both facts, not the better one.

faq.question: Is Kisspeptin an approved medicine?
faq.answer: ChEMBL records CHEMBL376756 at maximum clinical phase 3, with no approval recorded. Approval status differs by jurisdiction and is pending human review on this record.

faq.question: Which species has Kisspeptin been studied in?
faq.answer: Studies in this record's ledger report work in: Dogs, Humans, Mice, Zebrafish. Findings in one species do not transfer to another, and weight-normalized doses in particular do not scale linearly between them.
